title: AA House
paragraphs: Set along a narrow street minutes from Bintaro Station, AA House is a calm retreat within a dense urban neighborhood. Guided by symmetry, simplicity, and the honest use of natural materials, it embraces light, shadow, and ventilation to feel both grounded and serene.

The house reflects the character of its owners, reserved from the outside yet warm and welcoming within. A restrained facade with limited openings and concealed entrances gives the street a quiet, private presence.

Beyond the entrance, the plan gradually opens around an inner courtyard, revealing a brighter and more inviting atmosphere. This courtyard becomes the heart of the home, bringing natural light, airflow, and a sense of calm to everyday life.

The living room, dining area, and kitchen sit between two small courtyards, keeping nature close to daily activities. Indoor and outdoor boundaries soften, creating a comfortable, breathable environment for a family of four.

title: AM House
paragraphs: AM House is a contemporary tropical residence designed around light, airflow, and material warmth. A central courtyard brings natural light deep into the home while promoting cross ventilation throughout the living spaces. Exposed red brick, timber finishes, and roster screens create a layered architectural language that balances openness with privacy.
Located within a dense residential neighborhood in Cinere, the project responds to the client's wish for a house that feels airy and connected while keeping a sense of comfort and privacy.

At the heart of the home, a light-filled courtyard acts as both a visual anchor and a source of natural ventilation, letting daylight reach deep into the interior and keeping a continuous dialogue between indoor and outdoor spaces.

The material palette is intentionally restrained. Exposed red brick introduces texture and warmth, timber finishes soften the spaces, and roster screens filter light and provide subtle layers of privacy, aging naturally to enrich the house over time.

title: Louver House
paragraphs: Louver House explores the beauty of repetition as an architectural expression. A series of timber louvers forms a protective layer around the home, filtering light, creating privacy, and establishing a calm rhythm across the facade. Paired with textured surfaces and restrained materials, the architecture embraces simplicity as a way to achieve warmth and permanence.
Responding to a vision of a home that is modern, grounded, and quietly elegant, the design explores how repetition can become an architectural language rather than a decorative element.

The facade is shaped by solid timber louvers that create depth, privacy, and a strong visual identity. Their repetition introduces order and calm while filtering sunlight, and through the day light and shadow move across the surfaces, bringing subtle variation to a restrained composition.

A palette of textured walls and natural timber reinforces the home's warm, tactile character, while generous roof overhangs answer the tropical climate, giving shade and strengthening the building's horizontal presence.

title: HY House
paragraphs: HY House Sentul is conceived as a retirement home for two homeowners entering a slower, more intentional stage of life. Built around their habit of hosting family and close friends, it balances openness and intimacy through a sequence of warm, connected spaces.

Rooted in Senawa's tropical approach, the project embraces natural ventilation, filtered daylight, and a strong relationship between indoor and outdoor living. Generous openings and shaded transitional areas let the house breathe and set a calm rhythm through the day.

The plan prioritizes comfort, accessibility, and ease of movement, while communal areas become the heart of the home for conversation, shared meals, and everyday rituals. Natural textures, muted tones, and tactile finishes give the spaces warmth and familiarity.

Rather than treating tropical architecture as a visual statement, the project interprets it quietly, through light, air, proportion, and the honest use of materials, for a home that feels grounded and serene.

title: TV House
paragraphs: A home in South Jakarta shaped by a bold mid-century modern character and a desire for warmth and intimacy.
The ground floor brings together the living, dining, and kitchen as one continuous space, while a mezzanine above introduces a small library for the children - a quiet place for reading and study.

With generous ceiling heights throughout, the challenge was to create a sense of calm and groundedness. The interior is therefore defined by a tactile palette of wood, terrazzo, rattan, and stone, bringing warmth and depth to the open volume.

Rather than treating each space as separate, the materials flow continuously throughout the interior, connecting the different areas into one cohesive whole. The result is a home designed around togetherness - a warm and intimate setting for a family that spends most of their days within its walls.

title: NSB PS
paragraphs: Designed for Noir Sur Blanc at Plaza Senayan, the interior explores the relationship between brand identity and spatial expression. Rather than competing with the brand's bold character, it works as a quiet backdrop, reduced to a single material and color palette of terracotta tones so the identity of Noir Sur Blanc takes center stage.

Terracotta was chosen for its warmth, depth, and tactile quality. Applied consistently across surfaces, it makes an immersive environment that feels grounded and memorable, where subtle shifts of light and shadow add richness without contrast or ornament.

The project treats restraint as a powerful gesture. By removing unnecessary visual noise, the space becomes a clear, confident setting where the bold personality of Noir Sur Blanc can unfold, supporting the brand rather than competing with it.

title: FR House
paragraphs:
Rooted in Mid-Century Modern Design, this interior explores the relationship between clean geometry, natural wood grain, and carefully layered materials.
Our clients, both doctors, spend much of their days working outside the home. They envisioned a space that could shift the pace of their daily lives - a place to unwind, recharge, and reconnect with their family after long hours of work.

The interior is shaped by a restrained palette of timber, muted tones, and tactile surfaces. Clean lines and softened forms create a natural sense of rhythm, while the interplay of materials brings depth without overwhelming the space. Rooted in Mid-Century Modern principles, the design finds its character in simplicity, thoughtful proportions, and the quiet balance between function and atmosphere.

title: K Villa
paragraphs: Nestled in the lush landscape of Ubud, the villa is designed around its most remarkable asset: uninterrupted views toward the rice terraces and river valley below. The architecture opens itself toward the horizon, letting the surrounding landscape become an integral part of everyday living.

Rather than competing with nature, the villa acts as a quiet frame for the scenery beyond. Large openings, shaded terraces, and an infinity pool are positioned to strengthen the connection between interior and landscape, drawing the eye outward toward layered views of rice fields, flowing water, and tropical vegetation.

The concept balances openness with a sense of grounding. While the architecture reaches toward the horizon, its materiality stays rooted in place, with exposed solid timber, traditional shingle roofing, natural stone, and handcrafted details that bring warmth, texture, and authenticity.

Responding to Bali's tropical climate, deep overhangs, natural ventilation, and generous semi-outdoor spaces blur the boundary between inside and outside, letting light, air, and nature move freely through the house.
